key_insight: WWL-GPR augmented with electronic-structure and local-environment descriptors predicts adsorbate and transition-state energies on doped ZrO2 surfaces better than linear scaling models, improving downstream methanol-yield screening.
engineering_relevance: This provides a more data-efficient surrogate for prioritizing dopants in CO2 hydrogenation catalyst design when full DFT screening is too expensive.
method: Attributed graph representation of adsorbate–surface structures on ZrO2(101).
Extended Wasserstein Weisfeiler-Lehman Gaussian Process Regression with surface-relevant features.
Benchmarked against thermodynamic scaling relations and Brønsted–Evans–Polanyi models, then propagated to microkinetic yield estimates.
evidence_signal: Across Al, Cd, Ga, In, and Zn dopants, the model improved intermediate energetics, produced competitive TS predictions, and gave CH3OH-yield estimates closer to DFT than the linear-relation workflow.
watch_item: Performance still depends on the quality and coverage of the training data, and microkinetic conclusions can shift if key rate-controlling steps are mispredicted.
paper_title: Improved screening of doped ZrO$_2$ catalysts for CO$_2$ hydrogenation from graph-based machine learning
